The attaching maps of a join

The mapping-out construction of a join glues a cylinder to its two endpoint categories. To construct the map induced by functors on those categories, the two attaching squares must be compared with their specified restrictions. We describe this calculation for absolute joins. Assume the Chapter 1 structures, including universal coproducts, the walking morphism and the mapping-out join axiom.

For \(C,D\), put \(W=C\times D\) and write \[ B=W\sqcup W,\qquad Z=W\times [1],\qquad E=C\sqcup D. \] Let \(\iota _e=(\operatorname {id}_W,e)\colon W\to Z\) be endpoint insertion. The two attaching maps are \[ t=[\iota _0,\iota _1]\colon B\to Z,\qquad b=[\operatorname {in}_C\operatorname {pr}_C, \operatorname {in}_D\operatorname {pr}_D]\colon B\to E. \]

Supplementary Lemma 1. The chosen join \(C\star D\) is the pushout of \(t\) and \(b\). Its boundary map \(a\colon E\to C\star D\) is the original join inclusion; its cylinder map \(j\colon Z\to C\star D\) carries a specified matching \(jt=ab\).

Proof idea

The comparison \(C\times D\to C\times _\star D\) is an equivalence with specified projection computations. Use it on the cylinder, and use distributivity to replace its boundary by two copies of \(W\). The projection computations identify the two attaching maps with \(t,b\). Transport the whole universal cocone through these equivalences. Finally identify its boundary leg with the original join inclusion and transport the matching along that identification. This gives the claimed pushout with its specified legs. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. For \(f\colon C\to C'\) and \(g\colon D\to D'\), put \(v=f\times g\), \(d=v\sqcup v\), \(z=v\times \operatorname {id}_{[1]}\) and \(e=f\sqcup g\). There are comparisons \[ t'd=zt,\qquad b'd=eb \] whose restrictions to the two summands are the endpoint-insertion and projection comparisons.

Proof idea

On each summand the first equation reduces to \(\iota '_{\varepsilon }v=z\iota _{\varepsilon }\) for \(\varepsilon =0,1\). Compare the product projections: the \(W'\) projection is \(v\) and the interval projection is the same constant endpoint. For the second equation, compute the \(C'\) and \(D'\) projections of \(f\times g\) and then apply the appropriate coproduct inclusion.

These calculations initially compare the restrictions of \(t'd,zt\) and \(b'd,eb\). Lift each pair through the equivalence on identification animae induced by coproduct restriction. Its two computation laws retain the specified comparisons on each summand. This is the prescribed-image coproduct calculation. □

Supplementary Lemma 3. There is a functor \(F\colon C\star D\to C'\star D'\) with comparisons \[ Fj=j'z,\qquad Fa=a'e, \] compatible with the specified matchings on \(B\).

Proof idea

Restrict the target join cocone along the three maps \(d,z,e\), using the two comparisons of Supplementary Lemma 2. This is a cocone on the source span. Extend it through the source pushout. The computation law of the extension compares the entire resulting cocone with the one just constructed. Its two components are the displayed identifications, and its matching equation is their required compatibility. □

This is the pushout-defined action on joins. The checked declarations linked here do not supply its identity and composition laws or identify it with the separate action constructed using dependent products. General associativity of joins is also outside the scope of this note.
